picks.file: Ayntab in the 19th century, from F. R. Chesney, The Expedition for the Survey of the Rivers Euphrates and Tigris, London 1850.jpg
picks.what: The town below its castle mound, engraving in F. R. Chesney’s Expedition for the Survey of the Rivers Euphrates and Tigris
picks.why: only historical general view: the castle on its mound above the town, minarets on the skyline; no margins to cut

gaps: P0–P3: nothing; P5: only portraits; the 1909 tent-camp photographs (#1–#3) are skipped
notes: #4 was probably drawn during Chesney’s expedition in the 1830s but is dated by its 1850 publication; the print is pale and low in contrast. #1–#3 (Bain News Service, 1909) show a refugee tent camp, not the town, and the identification is doubtful: #1 is captioned Aintab but #2, from the same set, is captioned “Refugee camp in Trans-Caucasus”. #8–#9 are museum interiors.
